Southeast Crescent Regional Commission (SCRC) Investing in South Carolina’s regional growth

Through SCRC, eligible South Carolina communities can pursue competitive grants for projects that strengthen infrastructure, expand economic opportunity and support long-term regional growth.

Connect with a grants expert

SCRC investment in South Carolina

The Southeast Crescent Regional Commission is a federal-state partnership supporting economic and community development across a seven-state region. SCRC invests in projects that address persistent economic challenges and help communities build the infrastructure, services and capacity needed for future growth.

In South Carolina, the program is administered by SC Commerce’s Business Incentives and Community Development division in coordination with the Governor’s Office and regional Councils of Governments. The state’s SCRC region includes 39 eligible counties.

Investment priorities

SCRC investment priorities

SCRC supports projects aligned with six regional investment priorities:

Critical infrastructure

Water, wastewater, transportation, broadband and other infrastructure needed to support communities and economic growth.

Healthcare and public access

Programs and facilities that improve access to healthcare, essential services and community support.

Workforce capacity

Education, training and workforce development initiatives that prepare residents for employment and strengthen local talent pipelines.

Economic opportunities

Business development, entrepreneurship and other initiatives that create jobs and expand economic opportunity.

Affordable housing

Projects that improve the availability, affordability and quality of housing across the region.

Conservation and preservation

Efforts that protect natural resources, encourage sustainable development and support recreation and tourism.

Eligibility

Who can apply?

Depending on the funding opportunity, eligible applicants may include:

  • State governments and agencies 
  • Local governments, including towns, cities and counties 
  • Other political subdivisions, including regional planning organizations and local government consortia 
  • Federally recognized tribes 
  • Eligible nonprofit organizations 

Projects must benefit an eligible area within South Carolina’s SCRC region. County economic designations may affect project eligibility, matching requirements and funding priority.

Funding opportunities

Funding opportunities

The State Economic and Infrastructure Development (SEID) Grant Program is SCRC’s primary competitive funding program. SEID supports construction and nonconstruction projects aligned with the Commission’s investment priorities.

Funding cycles, award amounts, matching requirements, deadlines and application materials may change with each round. When a South Carolina application cycle opens, the current funding notice and state-specific deadlines should be posted here.

Visit the SCRC grant portal
